blocks.text: `RUN --mount` gives a single build step temporary access to a persistent cache, a secret, or an SSH agent, none of which are committed to the image.

items: The layer still re-runs when its key changes; downloads are just reused.
Lives in the builder, not the image or registry; ephemeral runners start empty.
apt needs `sharing=locked` and removal of Debian's docker-clean hook.

blocks.text: Exists only for that RUN (file at /run/secrets/<id> or an env var); never in a layer or history.
`docker build --ssh default`: the agent is forwarded for one step; the key never enters the image.

Q: "How do you use a private package index in a Docker build without leaking the token?" A: "A BuildKit secret mount: RUN --mount=type=secret,id=... with docker build --secret. The secret exists only during that step. ARG, ENV and copy-then-delete all leave it in the image."

items: Cache mounts speed re-runs without bloating images.
Secret mounts are the only safe build-time secret.
SSH mounts for private git deps.
Builder cache isn't shared unless exported.
